statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 20% at the watch floor as NQ bounces about 166 points off the 30,684.50 session low to 30,850.00 on expanding volume, while a 10-year near 5.29%, Brent above 100 dollars and a dense midday data block keep Stress at 75%.
recommendation: Tail is unchanged at 20% and remains five points below the 25% block threshold. The preceding assessment recorded 30,834.75 with the overnight retracement deepened to roughly 313 points; price has since firmed about 15 points to 30,850.00, and the session low of 30,684.50 now stands about 166 points below the current level. That is the completed shape of a working retracement rather than the start of a one-way path, and it is the structural opposite of what the Tail score measures. No amplifier is observed. There is no session-extreme holding, no shallow-pullback sequence and no repeated extension after a failed retracement, while turnover has expanded again to about 146k contracts and VIX has eased to 16.36 from a 17.00 session high. Two readings improved this hour: Dow futures have recovered from roughly half a percent lower to 51,251.00, down 0.05%, so intra-equity dispersion has narrowed, and the Micron result identifies that dispersion as memory and semiconductor rotation rather than index-level structure. Stress accordingly eases one point to 75% while remaining high on the 5.29% 10-year, Brent at 100.589 dollars and the midday release stack. The 12:00-15:00Z danger window is unchanged and covers jobless claims at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open, the final manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing at 14:00Z, which is the range where observed post-release continuation would justify escalation.
headline: NQ firms to 30,850.00, holding about 166 points above the 30,684.50 session low with Tail at 20% as VIX eases to 16.36 and Micron-led semiconductor rotation narrows the Dow divergence
body: December E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures trade 30,850.00, up 151.25 points or 0.49% from the 30,698.75 settle, with a session range of 30,684.50 to 31,147.75 on about 146k contracts. A second independent venue corroborates the level at 30,851.75, so the price is well established. The development of this hour is that the overnight fade has stopped extending. The previous assessment recorded 30,834.75 after roughly 313 points of the 449-point overnight advance had been retraced; price has since firmed about 15 points and the session low of 30,684.50 was set before that, so NQ now stands roughly 166 points above the low and about 298 points below the 31,147.75 overnight high. It remains some 245 points below the 31,094.75 pivot that earlier assessments named as the marker of genuine uptrend resumption. A 463-point retracement from the high, followed by a partial bounce, on turnover that expanded from about 134k to about 146k contracts, is the complete signature of a functioning two-way book. The no-retracement path the Tail score is built to detect requires the opposite: directional efficiency on thinning participation. Volatility pricing agrees. VIX is 16.36, up 0.02 or 0.12% against a 16.34 close, with a 16.21 to 17.00 range, so the index has drifted back toward unchanged after an early push and sits at an absolute level that gives no support to a pathological-path score. The intra-equity dispersion flagged in the previous assessment has narrowed materially. Dow futures trade 51,251.00, down 27.00 points or 0.05%, having been lower by roughly half a percent an hour earlier, while S&P 500 futures are 7,730.00, up 14.50 or 0.19%, and Nasdaq-100 futures lead at 0.49%. The cause is now identifiable. Micron reported fiscal fourth-quarter results after Wednesday's close with earnings of 33.42 dollars per share against estimates near 31.83 dollars, revenue of 54.23 billion dollars against about 51.49 billion expected, and a raised first-quarter outlook. A memory and high-bandwidth-memory beat of that size lifts semiconductors and the Nasdaq-100 specifically, which explains why NQ outperforms a flat Dow. Identified sector rotation is a materially better reading than unexplained index dispersion: it lowers directional conviction for the index as a whole and belongs in Stress, and under the operative risk definition it does not raise Tail. Cross-asset conditions remain the principal source of difficulty. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.29%, up about four basis points from a 5.26% prior close and rising for a fourth consecutive session, near its highest in roughly nineteen years, with September delivering the largest monthly move in yields since September 2022. The Federal Reserve H.15 series corroborates the trend: the 10-year ran 5.11% on 23 September to 5.26% on 29 September while the 2-year moved 4.85% to 4.89%, so the curve continues to bear-steepen. Brent trades 100.589 dollars, up 2.61%, and WTI about 92.31 dollars, up 2.09%. Equities mixed to higher while the long end sells off and crude holds above 100 dollars is a genuine cross-asset conflict, and conflict of that character raises Stress and lowers conviction rather than raising Tail. The geopolitical channel was re-verified this hour and remains an unresolved negotiation rather than a discontinuity. As of 10:50Z, Iran's cabinet is considering a United States counterproposal to Tehran's seven-day plan for phasing the ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with the remaining disagreement over sequencing; a State Department spokesperson dismissed Iran's messaging while indirect talks continue through mediators. Alternate routing has restored Gulf exports to roughly 21.8 million barrels daily against about 23.3 million prewar. The headline risk is two-sided, since a sequencing agreement would be a crude-lower gap and a breakdown a crude-higher one, and two-sided headline risk belongs in Stress. The scheduled day ahead is dense and now more precisely specified. Initial jobless claims print at 12:30Z with consensus near 201K after a 197K prior, alongside continuing claims near 1,730K after 1,719K. The cash open follows at 13:30Z, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z with consensus near 57.0 against a 53.9 prior, and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus near 54.8 against 54.6. September non-farm payrolls, the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings follow at 12:30Z on 2 October, roughly two and a half hours beyond the end of this forecast window. None of these is treated as an automatic Tail escalation. The 7 August precedent is directly on point: a large payrolls surprise did not become a lethal no-retracement path, so event importance and dispersion are scored through Stress and Confidence until an observed price path says otherwise. One event carried by previous assessments has been removed. A Federal Reserve speaker appearance at 13:05Z could not be re-verified against the Richmond Fed speech listing or any primary schedule in this run, and the contract requires omitting an event whose timing is materially uncertain rather than carrying it forward, so it is absent from the calendar and from the danger-window reasoning. The window itself is unchanged at 12:00-15:00Z and remains fully justified by claims, the cash open, the final PMI and ISM. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and was not used as material evidence. Its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly 36 hours old and far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collection status is partial. Stale supporting context cannot establish current structure, so this assessment rests entirely on independent current research. Confidence is 88%. NQ is corroborated across two venues, VIX and the 10-year carry live quotes, the 2-year is anchored to the 29 September H.15 print, Brent and WTI are confirmed against two sources, the Micron result is verified across three independent reports, the release consensus figures are taken from a current preview, the Gulf negotiation state is verified against reporting timestamped inside this hour, and the seven-day calendar is checked with one unverifiable entry removed. The material gaps remain the stale shared context file and the absence of a live 2-year quote, which together are a small completeness deduction against an otherwise current evidence set.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 16% in the late-European hour of 30 September with the mode mixed, stepped into the watch band at 20% from 12:00Z as the US data block and the long-end selloff developed, and peaked at 23% around 15:00-16:00Z. It held 20-22% through the US afternoon and the early Asian session, then firmed steadily from 20% at 00:00Z through 21%, 22% and 23% to 24% at 05:00Z and 25% at 06:00Z, the only orange slot in the window, as NQ printed successive fresh overnight highs and accepted above the 31,094.75 pivot, with the mode turning trend-up across those two slots. The 07:00Z slot returned to 22% and the mixed mode once the first liquid two-way test produced a 188-point retracement, and 08:00Z through 10:00Z held 20% as that retracement extended past 400 points on expanding turnover. Stress rose almost monotonically across the period from 69% to 76%, and Confidence held 85-88% throughout.
outlookSummary: The danger window is unchanged at 12:00-15:00Z, covering initial and continuing jobless claims at 12:30Z against consensus near 201K after 197K and 1,730K after 1,719K, the 13:30Z cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z with consensus near 57.0 against a 53.9 prior, and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus near 54.8 against 54.6. A previously carried 13:05Z Federal Reserve speaker slot has been dropped because its timing could not be re-verified. Forecast Tail opens at 20% at the watch floor, firms to 21% into the claims hour and 22% across the cash open and final PMI, and peaks at the top of the watch band at 24% in the 14:00Z ISM hour where Stress tops at 79%. It decays to 21-23% through the US afternoon, firms a point to 22% into the power hour, and eases to 20-21% around the 20:00Z cash close and through the quiet post-close and early Asian hours, where Stress reaches its forecast-day low of 72%. It then firms through the later Asian session and the European pre-open to 22-23% and returns to 24% across the European morning as positioning concentrates ahead of September non-farm payrolls at 12:30Z on 2 October, roughly two and a half hours after this window ends. The whole forecast path stays inside the watch band and no slot reaches the 25% block threshold, because scheduled event importance and dispersion are scored through Stress and Confidence rather than through Tail until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure. Confidence decays from 88% to 82% with forecast distance and recovers to 84% once European cash hours restore observable structure.
